newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end flat in lacklustre trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end flat in lacklustre trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed almost unchanged on Sunday in lucklustre trading as investors opted for the sidelines, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares ended up 0.07 percent, or 0.21 points, to 285.71 on low all-share turnover of 117 million shekels against 150 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.05 percent higher at 293.18.
"Investors are waiting to see what will happen with the shekel on Monday and for the new cabinet appointments," said a trader at Tachlit Securities.

The shekel plunged five percent last week after the cabinet announced a reform of the exchange rate regime and the Bank of Israel lowered the base rate by a steep 1.2 percentage points to 12.7 percent.

The government narrowly survived a parliamentary no-confidence vote last week in which one-sixth of the coalition partners failed to support the government. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's fractious cabinet is still squabbling over a ministerial shake-up expected this week, which is expected to include Ariel Sharon's appointment as finance minister.
"The fact that the market did not plunge after the last political turmoil shows that it is still strong and the positive trend will continue," said Elisha Rosenfeld of Lehava Investments.

"If the dollar remains stable and nothing dramatic happens in politics I believe that the market will resume its rise in the coming days. The trend is still positive but investors prefer to sit back and wait for further developments," the Tachlit trader said.
Rosenfeld added that the market was waiting to see what overseas investors would do on Monday. "The foreigners are leading the market now," he said.

The most active shares were Bank Hapoalim, which fell 0.5 percent to 756 agorot on volume of 6.5 million shekels; Israel Chemicals, which rose 1.5 percent to 423 agorot on turnover of 5.8 million shekels; and Koor Industries, which gained 0.25 percent to 32,144 agorot on volume of 4.9 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
